text:
Russian and Ukrainian delegates have gathered in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for a new round of U.S.-mediated peace talks, though expectations for a breakthrough remain low as Russia appears determined to continue fighting rather than negotiate a settlement to the war, now in its fifth year.
White House special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are once again mediating the talks, which last through Wednesday. Both men have held a series of meetings with officials across Europe and Russia in recent weeks as they engage in a renewed charge of shuttle diplomacy.
Delegates from Russia and Ukraine last met in Geneva in February, though negotiations were put on hold following the outbreak of the U.S. Israel war against Iran. Since then, Ukraine and Russia have dramatically ramped up their attacks on each other ’s territory, inflicting significant economic pain and a growing human toll.
Kremlin adviser Vladimir Medinsky, an arch-conservative who previously served as Russia’s culture minister, is again serving as the chief negotiator of the Russian delegation. The team also includes senior military and intelligence officials.
Shortly before Tuesday’s opening session with Russian officials, Ukrainian delegates met with European and NATO representatives. Ukraine’s chief negotiator, Rustem Umerov, posted a photograph of the sit-down on Telegram, noting that officials gathered to “align our positions and coordinate steps ahead of the next phase of talks. ”
The primary focus of the latest round of negotiations, Umerov wrote , includes a “cessation of hostilities, reliable post-war security guarantees, Ukraine’s economic recovery and development, as well as humanitarian steps. ”
A source in Russia’s delegation told Reuters that Moscow hopes the Abu Dhabi talks will lay the groundwork for key elements of a post-war security framework for Europe.
U.S. officials also told the Financial Times that they are looking to resolve the Ukraine war and broader security arrangements for the continent in tandem, but emphasized that European officials should have a seat at the table, something that Moscow has so far rejected .
